## Why clean income at all

Self-reported household income in the LISS panel contains a familiar
family of artefacts: misplaced decimal points, monthly amounts entered
in an annual field, personal income entered in the household field,
placeholder values, sign errors, and residual SPSS missing codes. Left
in place, a single misplaced zero moves a household across every income
bracket an analysis uses.

`liss_clean_income()` turns the cleaning procedures that used to live
in ad hoc analysis scripts into a rule-driven, fully audited stage of
the lissr pipeline. Every decision rule is declared in a YAML ruleset,
every applied decision lands in a ledger with its evidence and a
plain-language justification, the original values stay in the returned
data, and a generated report lets any reader reconstruct and contest
each modification.

## Source nonresponse before numerical cleaning

The default source guard selects one reviewed household response:
`ci23p339 = -9999999999` in the verified English
`ci23p_EN_1.0p.sav` release. This is an encoded nonresponse, not an income
to rectify, scale or replace with a donor. Its answer subtype remains
`nonresponse_unknown`; questionnaire routing does not establish a definitive
don't-know or refusal label. Other CI fields, CA and CH contracts remain
outside this household contract. Explicit taxable and collection selections are
described below.

The recipe selects this exact reviewed contract from a versioned,
package-owned registry. Package code pins the registry's content digest and
compares the complete typed recipe record with its approved entry. Changing
a recipe, adding a field or supplying a new hash does not approve new scope.
Missing, corrupt or unapproved registry records block guarded processing;
the registry is not discovered from the working directory or fetched online.
CI23p337/338 have separate approved field records and require explicit selection;
they do not inherit household consumer approval.

Keep the complete carrier when source-result classes or source/readiness
attributes are retained. The cleaner rejects those markers without a carrier
before unwrapping, target resolution or preparation, including on scalar frames.
Carrier-free legacy wrapper readiness for unevaluated source scope remains a
nonclaiming hint and does not approve source exclusion. This preserves actual
absent-wave merge behavior and ordinary unguarded cleaner results.

Report writing and panel merging also reject source classes or source/readiness
attributes on the outer result or its selected inner frame. A partially named
data wrapper cannot discard scalar source lineage through either path. Ordinary
and absent-wave wrapper readiness retain their existing behavior. Guarded report
export and panel lineage propagation remain unsupported.

Enable the guard explicitly for an in-memory CI merge:

```{r source-nonresponse-merge}
guarded <- lissr::merge_liss_module(
  lissr::liss_recipe("ci"), data_dir = "data/ci",
  output_dir = NULL, source_nonresponse = TRUE
)
dry_guarded <- lissr::liss_clean_income(
  guarded, variables = list(target = "s339"), mode = "flag"
)
```

The merge verifies the exact source filename and SHA256, captures the raw
cell and field metadata before harmonization, and exposes a missing analysis
amount. Its `source_nonresponse` carrier records source identity, typed
classification, original values and scoped readiness. The cleaner consumes
that carrier before constructing numerical target or context vectors.
It also checks the reviewed household-income consumer approval, construct,
unit, measurement period and target binding. Passing source classification
alone does not authorize a different cleaner or establish that another
column is household income.
Matched cells cannot receive finite proposals, enter the covered numerical
roles or be revived by `disable`, `enable_only` or numerical parameter
overrides. The older `valid_for_analysis` flag retains its existing meaning;
it does not certify source nonresponse coverage. A source-bound household
amount cannot also be assigned as `category_code`; bracket categories need a
separate variable.

A raw or legacy merged frame needs an explicit rebind against the original
verified source. For example, first retain an ordinary in-memory merge result,
then bind its unchanged household target with the exact source wave column:

```{r source-nonresponse-rebind}
legacy_merge <- lissr::merge_liss_module(
  lissr::liss_recipe("ci"), data_dir = "data/ci", output_dir = NULL
)
bound <- lissr::liss_classify_source_nonresponse(
  legacy_merge,
  source = "data/ci/ci23p_EN_1.0p.sav",
  target = "s339", wave_col = "wave_id"
)
dry_bound <- lissr::liss_clean_income(
  bound, variables = list(target = "s339"), mode = "flag"
)
```

Pass the complete classifier wrapper `bound` to the cleaner. The classifier
does not add a frame marker to its unchanged `bound$data`: cleaning that
unmarked frame alone enters ordinary unguarded processing and makes no
source-nonresponse guarantee. Keep `legacy_merge` separately for its original provenance, log and
validation; those fields are not forwarded into `bound`.

Binding requires unique respondent keys and unchanged selected values;
a suffix, calendar year, filename assertion or legacy merge provenance is
insufficient. Reviewed target names are `ci23p339`, `s339`, `ci_s339`, `nethh`
and `ci00a339`;
an unapproved target name is rejected even if selected values happen to coincide.
An approved name and value agreement do not establish unforgeable field origin.
For a merged binding, every presented row needs a nonmissing, nonempty exact
wave ID, including rows outside `ci23p`. Full-join panels with CI-absent rows lacking CI wave identity
are unsupported, including when the selected target is `ci_s339`.
The binder preserves the caller's input. Flag mode preserves the actual supplied
target, including normalized missing values from a guarded merge, and reports
a missing proposed amount. Verified source originals are recovered only into
the `_observed` audit column and source ledger. Applied modes return a missing
target for matched cells while retaining that audit. Ordinary unmatched
responses retain the existing numerical policies, including the cleaner's
sign policy. Default target aliases do not expand automatically.

Sorting and subsetting remain usable through verified respondent and wave keys
when column metadata and the complete carrier are retained, as with supported
tibble/dplyr operations. Base data-frame operations that strip target attributes
fail closed; the metadata validator is not relaxed. Changed values, missing
lineage or altered audit metadata also block the guard. RDS preserves the carrier
and its integrity checks. The one-field version-1 carrier and public interface
remain unchanged: old valid RDS carriers are checked against the reviewed
contract without adding registry metadata or migrating the saved object.
Registry and carrier digests check integrity, not authentication or an
unforgeable field origin. The consumer gate relies on an intact validated
contract; it cannot recover lineage stripped from a bare frame.
Guarded merges require `output_dir = NULL`, and
cross-module panel merging is blocked for guarded results in this slice.
SAV/CSV exports with verified sidecars and automatic panel propagation are
deferred; an ordinary SAV or CSV file does not preserve this readiness.
Guarded cleaner reports also require `output_dir = NULL`; the existing report
writer cannot yet export the complete source audit.
Legacy workflows without the guard remain available and make no new source
nonresponse guarantee.

The returned readiness is scoped to this reviewed source and household field.
It does not make the source originals in `_observed` or other audit columns
suitable for quantitative analysis; use the missing analysis amounts and
proposals for quantitative review.

## Explicit taxable classification and normalization

Taxable CI23p337 (respondent taxable income) and CI23p338 (its estimated
follow-up) concern EUR amounts for 2022. Each can be selected explicitly by
one complete reviewed field mirror in a schema 2.0.0 recipe. The default CI
recipe and `recipe = NULL` still select legacy household field 339.

```{r taxable-source-selection}
reviewed_registry <- yaml::yaml.load_file(system.file(
  "schema", "source_nonresponse_registry.yml", package = "lissr"
))
selected_fields <- Filter(function(field) field$field_id == "CI23P337_FIELD",
                          reviewed_registry$fields)
stopifnot(length(selected_fields) == 1L)
tax_recipe <- lissr::liss_recipe("ci")
tax_recipe$source_nonresponse <- list(
  schema_version = "2.0.0", field = selected_fields[[1L]]
)
tax_audit <- lissr::liss_classify_source_nonresponse(
  legacy_merge, source = "data/ci/ci23p_EN_1.0p.sav", target = "s337",
  wave_col = "wave_id", recipe = tax_recipe
)
tax_normalized <- lissr::merge_liss_module(
  tax_recipe, data_dir = "data/ci", output_dir = NULL,
  source_nonresponse = TRUE
)
```

The audit leaves data values and metadata unchanged (`normalized = FALSE`).
The guarded merge replaces only the selected field's exact `-9999999999.0`
and `-9999999998.0` cases with missing analysis amounts (`normalized = TRUE`).
One version-2 carrier contains one field, one coverage/input receipt and a
ledger with distinct N01/N02 case IDs. Readiness includes per-case counts;
unknown answer subtypes remain `nonresponse_unknown`, with no numerical
proposal. Original missing-value attributes are retained and checked per code.
226/229 responses cannot resolve taxable subtypes or become amount estimates.
Signed/zero amounts, near codes and unselected fields retain existing behavior.

Select `CI23P338_FIELD` in a separate call for the estimated taxable amount.
The scalar classifier rejects collection recipes and simultaneous selection.
Approved taxable names
are the selected raw name, `s337`/`s338` or `ci_s337`/`ci_s338`; aliases never
establish source ownership. Existing guarded inputs cannot be rebound to a tax
field, and version-2 lineage cannot be rebound to legacy 339. Keep the complete
carrier for supported metadata-preserving subsets, reordering and RDS.

`liss_clean_income()` rejects taxable carriers before target resolution,
Background/P01 or numerical preparation under every mode and override, even
when a column is renamed to a household alias. Taxable readiness does not
certify household field 339 or approve taxable numerical cleaning. Source and
carrier digests check integrity; they cannot recover origin after all markers
are stripped or authenticate manually forged/resealed objects. Household
projection, CA20g/CH and portable guarded exports remain deferred.

## Joint taxable normalization in one guarded merge

A schema 3.0.0 recipe explicitly selects the complete reviewed 337/338 pair.
Guarded module merging supports this collection; the standalone classifier
remains scalar and rejects collection recipes.

```{r joint-taxable-selection}
joint_recipe <- lissr::liss_recipe("ci")
joint_recipe$source_nonresponse <- list(
  schema_version = "3.0.0", fields = unname(reviewed_registry$fields)
)
joint_taxable <- lissr::merge_liss_module(
  joint_recipe, data_dir = "data/ci", output_dir = NULL,
  source_nonresponse = TRUE
)
joint_taxable$source_nonresponse_readiness
```

Both complete mirrors must match package authority. Either selection order is
accepted and retained; missing, duplicate, extra or altered fields block. Both
source receipts must pass against unchanged original values before either
field is normalized. Both final receipts must pass after metadata restoration
and name cleanup before a collection is attached. Failure returns no partial
guarded result or file.

The singular `source_nonresponse` slot holds one tagged schema-3 collection
with the common source and two named complete sealed schema-2 states under
`fields`. Readiness retains actual per-case counts and sums field-cells. The
4,905-row source contributes 9,810 evaluated field-cells and 2,680 plus 1,389
classified cells, totaling 4,069 field-cells, not a respondent union. Valid
present fields pass even with zero matches. The entire shared wave absent is
`not_evaluated`; a present source missing either required field blocks.

Keep the complete collection for RDS and metadata-preserving subsets/reordering.
Validation checks both leaf receipts and outer integrity and reseals returned
state without changing the saved input. Unknown versions, incomplete carriers,
field replacement/drop and lost target metadata block. No scalar migration,
implicit first-field selection, household projection or new standalone collection
classifier is provided.

Schema-3 collections are rejected by the household cleaner before target/rules/P01 or
numeric preparation under all modes/overrides. Unselected 339 is not certified
by taxable readiness. Scalar rebinding rejects collection carriers and
readiness/class claims, even with the carrier removed. Reports, panels and
guarded exports remain unsupported. Stripping every marker loses lineage;
digests do not authenticate manually forged objects.

## Joint three-field normalization with native scalar receipts

Schema 4.0.0 explicitly selects exactly CI23p337, CI23p338 and CI23p339.
The package separately pins `source_nonresponse_collection_adapter.yml`, which
links `CI23P339_FIELD` to the existing `CI23P339_N01` rule. Registry 2 remains
the authority for all source, code, binding and evidence details. The adapter
is required only for schema 4; old scalar and two-field paths remain independent
of that new resource. Recipes select complete existing scalar blocks:

```{r joint-three-field-selection}
three_recipe <- lissr::liss_recipe("ci")
three_fields <- lapply(reviewed_registry$fields, function(field) list(
  field_id = field$field_id,
  scalar = list(schema_version = "2.0.0", field = field)
))
household_records <- Filter(function(record) {
  identical(record$contract$rule_id, "CI23P339_N01")
}, reviewed_registry$records)
stopifnot(length(household_records) == 1L)
three_fields[[3L]] <- list(
  field_id = "CI23P339_FIELD",
  scalar = list(schema_version = "1.0.0",
                contracts = list(household_records[[1L]]$contract))
)
three_recipe$source_nonresponse <- list(
  schema_version = "4.0.0", fields = three_fields
)
three_guarded <- lissr::merge_liss_module(
  three_recipe, data_dir = "data/ci", output_dir = NULL,
  source_nonresponse = TRUE
)
```

All six member orders are accepted and retained. All three unchanged original
receipts and normalization locks must pass before any amount column changes;
all three finalizers must pass before one complete collection is attached.
The `fields` members retain complete native version-2 taxable states and the
complete version-1 household state, including its original rule and 229 routing
candidate evidence. No scalar object is migrated or relabelled. Household 339
has only its existing exact `-9999999999.0` case; the second taxable code is not
a household case. Authority comes from the pinned adapter and registry, never
from an alias or list position.

The version-4 boundary checks all three restored canonical metadata, complete
source row/wave/key sets, receipts and ledgers. Every normalized classified
amount must stay missing, including 339. Original 229 routing supports a
candidate only; authoritative household subtype remains unknown. The native
household receipt has no separate original 229 vector, so coverage alone cannot
reconstruct that routing or authenticate a manually resealed object.

Readiness counts field-cells, retaining all three native per-field records and
actual case identities. Valid fields with zero matches pass. An entirely absent
shared wave is `not_evaluated` with no carrier and three zero-count records;
a present source missing any required field blocks the whole call. RDS and
metadata-preserving subsets/reordering validate every leaf and reseal returned
state without changing the saved input. Incomplete, contradictory, dropped or
replaced carriers and lost metadata block.

Separate pinned consumer policies permit the explicit household flag operation
and the applied-result operation described below. A household leaf's scalar
approval and source readiness do not grant either collection permission.
Corrected output uses a separate lineage contract because household cleaning can
change values bound by the source receipt. Scalar classification rejects schema
4, and scalar rebinding rejects
every claimed collection before discarding lineage. Guarded reports, panels
and SAV/CSV export remain unsupported. Defaults, scalar versions 1/2 and the
exact two-field version-3 contract retain their behavior; CA20g/CH remain deferred.

## Household flag simulation with the complete collection

The package-owned `source_nonresponse_collection_consumers.yml` policy grants
one operation on an intact version-4 collection. Select the target explicitly
through the existing argument and keep the complete result:

```{r collection-household-flag}
three_flag <- lissr::liss_clean_income(
  three_guarded, mode = "flag", variables = list(target = "s339"),
  output_dir = NULL
)
saveRDS(three_flag, "three_field_household_flag.rds")
```

All original columns, values, attributes and row order remain unchanged. The
complete three-field carrier stays on the result and frame. Native339 validation
recovers observed codes only into `s339_observed` and keeps classified339
`s339_proposed` values missing. Ordinary proposals use the existing flag rules.
This simulation does not apply corrections or establish numerical-model validity.

This FLAG capability does not cover correct/na_only; the distinct applied-result
path below covers those modes. Omitted or alias-based target selection and taxable
targets remain blocked. All three bound amount columns are prohibited in every secondary
role, including personal-income predictors, household grouping, bounds and donor
keys. These checks run before and after P01. Background must be an unguarded
frame or NULL; every guarded/claimed background is rejected before conversion,
even with disabled P01. Reserved P01 helper names and preexisting household audit
columns block, so added context or audit output cannot overwrite original columns.

Complete source validation runs before preparation, after P01 and on output.
Valid source-input subsets/reorder/RDS include empty and other-wave-only bound
frames. Zero household source evaluation keeps readiness `not_evaluated`; it
does not prevent ordinary other-wave flag simulation or certify other waves.
A result with no bound carrier cannot use this path.

The wrapper's separate `source_nonresponse_consumer_readiness` record binds the
full carrier digest and complete produced data, decisions, effective ruleset,
resolved variables, mode and summary except duration_s. The entire log is outside
the proof. Native three-field source readiness remains separate. The wrapper
has class `liss_clean_collection_flag_result`; its frame has source lineage only.
Validating `$data` alone cannot validate edited proposals or decisions.

Preserve the complete wrapper with RDS. Post-consumer subset/reorder and repeat
cleaning are not resealed; supply a supported source subset before a new flag
run. Source/consumer class-only or record-only claims still block rebinding and
exports. Digests detect unresealed changes, not manually forged objects, source
origin after every marker is stripped, or origin of copied unmarked predictors.
This FLAG operation introduces no public scalar projection, taxable consumer or
wider source scope.

## Applied household amounts with retained collection lineage

The separate `source_nonresponse_collection_applied.yml` policy permits a whole
applied result for the same explicit household target. Background attachment and
file/report output are excluded from this capability:

```{r collection-household-applied}
three_correct <- lissr::liss_clean_income(
  three_guarded, mode = "correct", variables = list(target = "s339"),
  background = NULL, output_dir = NULL
)
lissr::liss_validate_applied_income(three_correct)
saveRDS(three_correct, "three_field_household_applied.rds")
three_reloaded <- readRDS("three_field_household_applied.rds")
lissr::liss_validate_applied_income(three_reloaded, replay = TRUE)
```

`source_input` retains the exact accepted source collection and all three native
leaves. `data` contains the derived `s339` amount plus household audit columns;
both tax fields and every other original column retain their values, attributes
and order. Native source receipts are never rewritten to attest corrected
amounts. The separate `applied_lineage` record binds source, effective rules,
invocation, decisions, stable log/summary, metadata and output. Preserve the
complete result; the analysis frame alone cannot validate this relationship.

Source-classified household cells remain missing under every mode and override,
with raw codes recovered only in `s339_observed` and the retained source audit.
`na_only` uses the existing cleaner: preparation can rectify signs, and an explicit
F01 winsorisation override can produce a finite capped amount. It is not always
a finite-to-missing-only operation. The numerical method itself is unchanged.

Checked scoped source readiness is separate from analysis execution. A supported
source view containing only ordinary other-wave rows can run analysis while its
CI23p readiness remains `not_evaluated`. Its exact retained parent may contain
broader source receipts; those broader counts do not become current scope counts.
Raw-source metadata in native leaves, normalized input target metadata and derived
target metadata are distinct; the applied numeric target retains its label under
the existing cleaner's metadata rule.

Validation without replay checks typed whole-result integrity and source locks;
an ordinary digest is not authenticated execution. `replay = TRUE` additionally
requires the recorded computation identity/runtime and reproduces the captured
invocation from `source_input`. It does not reread original sources or validate
the statistical suitability of a correction. Engine/runtime changes can prevent
replay even when structural checks remain available.

Decision columns, optional dataset flags, summaries and log entries must retain
their constructor-owned types and field sets. Counts cannot be character values
or fractional numbers. Durations and timestamps still require valid scalar
types when their values are excluded from semantic replay. These shape checks
also apply to otherwise valid older whole-result RDS objects.

Manual output subsets/reorders, extracted analysis frames, background attachment,
second cleaning, reports, panels and SAV/CSV export remain unsupported. Start a
separate new run explicitly from the original `source_input`. Recognized applied
claims on wrappers or selected frames block lineage-discarding routes; deliberately
removing every class and marker leaves ordinary input of unknown ownership.

### Controlled views of existing applied output

Use the separate applied-view capability to select explicit parent row keys
without rerunning the cleaner on selected rows:

```{r collection-household-applied-view}
selected_keys <- rev(three_correct$applied_lineage$row_keys)
three_view <- lissr::liss_create_applied_income_view(three_correct, selected_keys)
lissr::liss_validate_applied_income_view(three_view)
saveRDS(three_view, "three_field_household_applied_view.rds")
view_reloaded <- readRDS("three_field_household_applied_view.rds")
lissr::liss_validate_applied_income_view(view_reloaded, replay = TRUE)
```

The view retains the exact complete applied result, including original native
source input, in `parent_result`. Supply ordered unique plain character row keys;
`character(0)` explicitly requests an empty view. Every data column stays in
parent order, with natural selected names/dimensions and unchanged descriptive
metadata. Source locks, tax amounts and audit/status columns are projected as
already computed. The separate version-1 view policy and lineage do not change
the native version-4 carrier or the existing whole-parent computation identity.

The projected decisions retain original root `row` and opaque `decision_id`,
then append integer `root_decision_row` and `view_row`. References use the complete
parent digest plus root ledger ordinal; repeated decision IDs are allowed.
Entries are ordered by view row and root ledger ordinal. Row and decision counts
are distinct because one selected row can have several decisions.

`view_status` records projection only. Scoped `source_readiness` is checked from
selected ORIGINAL source rows with their unchanged receipt. Parent readiness and
analysis execution status remain separate. Empty or other-wave-only selections
can have `not_evaluated` source scope while the parent completed analysis.

Validation reconstructs the exact closed projection. Optional replay executes
the complete parent under its existing runtime gate, never a selected-row refit.
Whole-view RDS is supported; whole-parent validation rejects a view wrapper.
Nested views, repeated cleaning, source rebinding, background attachment,
report/panel consumption and SAV/CSV export remain unsupported. Ordinary hashes
are not authentication: coordinated resealing can describe another consistent
parent/view, and permitted nonsemantic parent timing changes can pass both
validation modes. Replay does not establish source authenticity or statistical
validity. Retain the complete object and its recognized guarded claims.

## The ruleset

The default ruleset ships with the package and is the single source of
truth for what the cleaner may do:

```{r ruleset}
library(lissr)

rs <- liss_cleaning_ruleset()
print(rs)

system.file("cleaning", "income_cleaning_rules.yml", package = "lissr")
```

Rules are grouped into four sections. Preparation rules (P01 to P06)
resolve columns, attach background demographics, expand bracket codes,
rectify sign errors, and sweep residual SPSS missing codes. Detection
rules (D01 to D11) identify implausible cells, from unrecoverable
placeholder values through household-level scale errors and robust
statistical outliers to dataset-level extremes. Correction rules (C01
to C06) generate candidate replacement values. The finalization rule
(F01) handles anything still outside the plausible range according to
its `disposition`: `void` (the default) sets such values to NA,
`winsorise` clamps over-cap values to the cap, and `flag` only ledgers
them. Each rule carries an id, a description, a rationale, optional
literature references, parameters, and an `enabled` switch.

## Quick start: dry run first, then correct

The cleaner operates on merged module output. A dry run in `"flag"`
mode performs the full procedure without touching a single value; the
simulated result arrives in `nethh_proposed` and every would-be
decision in the ledger:

```{r flag-mode}
result <- merge_liss_module(liss_recipe("ci"), data_dir = "data/ci",
                            output_dir = "output/ci")

dry <- liss_clean_income(result, mode = "flag")

head(dry$decisions)
summary(dry)
```

Once the proposals look right, run in the default `"correct"` mode and
write the audit artifacts:

```{r correct-mode}
cleaned <- liss_clean_income(result, output_dir = "output/ci")

cleaned$data$nethh          # cleaned values
cleaned$data$nethh_observed # untouched input, always preserved
table(cleaned$data$nethh_clean_status, useNA = "ifany")
```

A third mode, `"na_only"`, voids detected cells without imputing
anything, for analyses that prefer missingness over model-based
corrections.

## Reading a decision

Every modified cell has at least one ledger row. A scale-error
correction looks like this:

```{r ledger}
d <- cleaned$decisions
d[d$rule_id == "D06", c("person_id", "wave", "observed", "corrected",
                        "candidate_source", "evidence")]

# the justification column carries the full sentence, for example:
# "detected by scale_error; replaced with the household_median candidate
#  25800 (closest of 4 admissible candidate(s) to the household_median
#  25800; constrained to [8000, 150000])"
```

The `candidates` column lists every admissible candidate the selection
saw, so a reader can verify that the applied value was the closest to
the anchor, and the `valid_min`/`valid_max` columns show the constraint
window (category bounds where reported, global limits otherwise).

## The report

`liss_cleaning_report()` renders three artifacts: a markdown report
whose methodology section is generated from the ruleset itself (every
rule with its description, rationale, parameters, and references), the
complete decision ledger as CSV, and an engine-shaped JSONL audit log:

```{r report}
liss_cleaning_report(cleaned, output_dir = "output/ci")
```

Because the methodology is generated from the ruleset that actually
ran, the report can never drift from the code.

## Disagreeing with a rule

Every rule can be switched off or re-parameterised per run, and the
overrides are recorded in the report:

```{r overrides}
# a stricter volatility requirement for scale-error detection,
# no extreme-z net, and a higher plausibility cap
cleaned2 <- liss_clean_income(
  result,
  income_cap = 175000,
  disable = c("D10"),
  params = list(D06 = list(volatility_min = 0.7))
)
```

For a lasting policy, copy the packaged YAML, edit it, and pass the
path; `validate_cleaning_ruleset()` enforces the schema:

```{r custom-ruleset}
cleaned3 <- liss_clean_income(result, ruleset = "my_income_rules.yml")
```

## Attaching background demographics

Donor-pool matching (correction rule C05) works best with household
size, position, occupation, age, and education attached. Rule P01
aligns a monthly background file to the annual wave scale, keeps one
row per person-year, and joins on the person id, never on the household
id:

```{r background}
background <- haven::read_sav("data/avars_201801_EN_1.0p.sav")
cleaned <- liss_clean_income(result, background = background)
```

## Equivalised income

For cross-household comparison, `liss_equivalise_income()` provides the
scale the source analysis pipelines used, alongside the OECD-modified
and square-root alternatives:

```{r equivalise}
library(magrittr)

panel <- cleaned$data %>%
  dplyr::mutate(
    stand_inc = liss_equivalise_income(nethh, aantalhh, aantalki)
  )
```

One definitional caveat for the OECD-modified scale: it defines
children as household members under 14, while `aantalki` counts
children living at home of any age, so passing `aantalki` approximates
that scale; see `?liss_equivalise_income`.

## Where the rules came from

The ruleset consolidates the income-cleaning procedures of two
production analysis projects and corrects several latent defects found
while porting them. The declarative rules are maintained in
`inst/cleaning/income_cleaning_rules.yml`, with regression coverage in
`tests/testthat/test-clean-income.R`. Proposed rules and parameter changes
can be reviewed through pull requests.

## Assessment beyond household income

The [Data Quality Assessment Beyond Household Income](data-quality-assessment.html)
documents a completed investigation of the available core modules and
monthly Background Variables. It reports observed coding problems,
implausible values and logical inconsistencies, distinguishes defensible
corrections from review-only cases, and ranks future work using prevalence,
analytical impact and correction risk. It describes a roadmap; the
